newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo opposition leader in contact with Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Congo opposition leader in contact with Kabila.

text.p: Veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi said on Thursday he was in touch with President Laurent Kabila's Alliance to "harmonise conflicting views" on the Democratic Republic of the Congo's institutions.

He told a crowd of thousands of students at Kinshasa University that talks had begun last month, a week after Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo took power in the former Zaire.
"You will be pleased with the outcome of this dialogue. It will match the expectations of the people of this country. An eight-member commission has been set up," he said to cheers.

Kabila, who ousted veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in a seven-month rebellion, promptly banned all political parties save his Alliance and refused to offer ex-premier Tshisekedi, the most popular anti-Mobutu politician, a role in government.

Tshisekedi did not elaborate on the items under discussion but suggested that the contacts would lead to the formation of a new government and that he could soon meet Kabila for the first time since he declared himself president.
Kabila's Alliance dominates the current government.
"It will be a question of a transitional government to organise elections. This government will also solve the problem (of nationality) in eastern Congo," he said.
Ethnic strife has claimed thousands of lives in Kivu, in the east. It is not clear who is "Congolese" and who is not in these provinces bordering Rwanda and Burundi.
Kabila's Rwandan-backed rebellion began in Kivu in October.
Many of his Tutsi-dominated forces initially took up arms to claim the Zairean citizenship which Mobutu denied them.

"We have thanked our foreign friends who have helped us to get rid of the dictator in the final stage of our fight. But this objective has been achieved, now they (foreign friends) have to leave," Tshisekedi said, without further details.
Many Congolese say Rwandan, Ugandan and Burundian soldiers are in the ranks of the Alliance forces. The government has denied suggestions of a foreign presence in the new army.
